items.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001
items.q: We got to play with everybody in that place you know. Bill Harris came in, he was one of the featured —J.J. Johnson you know... he and I would go in all these after hour joints and hang out and play and stuff.

ctx.x: Another practical reason for doing something, right? © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

Right. So Billy and I were the house trio, Billy’s trio was at this place called the Downbeat, which used to be on 54th Street. And Oscar was a regular. We got to play with everybody in that place you know. Bill Harris came in, he was one of the featured —J.J. Johnson you know. We were the house trio. So I’d sit behind Oscar when he was playing. And then at night after the end of the gig, he and I would go in all these after hour joints and hang out and play and stuff.
Do you have copies of all the records you played on?
